verdict.rationale: The Gmail API offers OAuth scopes, and Google's docs tell developers to pick the narrowest scope and use non-sensitive scopes to limit an app to the features it needs. This gives a real least-privilege mechanism for agent credentials. Community reports say the scopes are coarse: roughly full control, read-all, everything-except-delete, or drafts-only, with no way to restrict access to a specific label. Missing for 10: label- or folder-level scoping, a documented user-facing flow for issuing and revoking per-agent credentials, and independent corroboration of fine-grained least-privilege.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Whenever possible, use non-sensitive scopes to narrow access to only the specific features needed by an app.
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Gmail API auth scopes already allow read-only access, but one user wants to restrict apps to a specific label or subfolder
